---
title: "Reveal.js presentations"
---

## Overview

Like other documents, a reveal.js presentation in Quarto is a Markdown document. Add `format: revealjs` to the document's front matter to choose the slideshow format:

```yaml
---
format: revealjs
---
```

From there, headings become slides and the document metadata becomes a
title slide. The rest of this page walks through the slide-authoring
features Quarto 2 supports today.

::: {.callout-note}
Quarto 2's reveal.js support is still growing. This page documents only what is
implemented now; features such as code-line highlighting, the speaker-view UI,
and the reveal.js plugins (menu, search, chalkboard) are not yet available.
:::

## Creating slides

A level-2 heading (`##`) starts a new slide, and the heading content becomes the slide title. A level-1 heading (`#`) starts a *section*, gathering the slides
beneath it into a vertical stack. A horizontal rule (`---`) starts a
new slide with no title.

:::: {#demo-creating-slides .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/01-creating-slides/slides.html"}
```markdown
---
title: "Habits"
author: "Jane Doe"
format: revealjs
---

## Getting up

- Turn off alarm
- Get out of bed

## Going to sleep

- Get in bed
- Count sheep
```

A minimal deck: the front matter becomes a title slide, and each `##`
heading starts a new slide. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/01-creating-slides)
::::

Sections and rule-delimited slides follow the same heading logic:

:::: {#demo-sections .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/02-sections/slides.html"}
```markdown
# Part One

## First topic

Content.

# Part Two

## Another topic

Content.

---

An untitled slide, created with a horizontal rule.
```

Level-1 headings build section stacks, and a horizontal rule starts an
untitled slide. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/02-sections)
::::

### The title slide

When the front matter carries a `title` metadata entry (and optionally, an `author` or `date` fields), Quarto will produce a title slide.

### Slide level

By default, level-2 headings make slides and level-1 headings make
sections. The `slide-level` option moves that boundary: with
`slide-level: 1`, level-1 headings become slides and there are no section
stacks.

```yaml
---
format:
  revealjs:
    slide-level: 1
---
```

## Fragments

A fragment reveals part of a slide on a later click instead of all at once.
Wrap the content in a `.fragment` div, and reveal.js holds it back until you
advance.

Variant classes such as `.fade-up`, `.fade-out`, `.grow`, and
`.highlight-red` change how a fragment animates in. To control the reveal
order independently of source order, set `fragment-index`:

```markdown
::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}
Shown second.
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}
Shown first.
:::
```

@demo-fragments puts a couple of fragments together in a runnable deck.

:::: {#demo-fragments .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/03-fragments/slides.html"}
```markdown
## Reveal on click

::: {.fragment}
Appears on the first click.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
Then this one fades up.
:::
```

Fragments reveal content one step at a time. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/03-fragments)
::::

## Incremental lists

Lists are a special case of fragments. To reveal every list in the deck one
item at a time, set `incremental` globally:

```yaml
---
format: revealjs
incremental: true
---
```

To override that choice for a single list, wrap it. A `.nonincremental` list
shows all its items at once even under the global setting, and an
`.incremental` list steps through its items even when the global setting is
off:

:::: {#demo-incremental-lists .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/04-incremental-lists/slides.html"}
```markdown
::: {.nonincremental}
- All three
- appear
- together.
:::
```

A `.nonincremental` list opts out of the deck's incremental reveal. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/04-incremental-lists)
::::

## Multiple columns

To place content side by side, use a `.columns` container holding two or more
`.column` divs. Each column's `width` sets its share of the row.

:::: {#demo-columns .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/05-columns/slides.html"}
```markdown
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
Left column.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
Right column.
:::

::::
```

Two columns sit side by side, each taking its share of the row. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/05-columns)
::::

## Speaker notes

A `.notes` div holds commentary for the presenter. The note does not appear
on the slide.

:::: {#demo-speaker-notes .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/06-speaker-notes/slides.html"}
```markdown
## A slide with notes

Slide content the audience sees.

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes go here.
:::
```

Speaker notes travel with the slide without appearing on it. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/06-speaker-notes)
::::

::: {.callout-note}
Speaker notes render today as a hidden `aside`; the live speaker view that
displays them while presenting is not yet available.
:::

## Asides

An aside holds content of more peripheral interest — a caveat, a citation, a
side remark. Quarto shows it small and muted at the bottom of the slide.

:::: {#demo-asides .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/07-asides/slides.html"}
```markdown
## A slide with an aside

The main point, front and center.

::: {.aside}
Some commentary of more peripheral interest.
:::
```

An aside sits small and muted at the bottom of the slide. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/07-asides)
::::

## Footnotes

Footnotes on a slide are gathered into an aside at the bottom of *that*
slide, rather than into a single list at the end of the deck. Each slide
numbers its own footnotes from one, and when a slide carries both an aside
and footnotes, they share a single block at the bottom.

:::: {#demo-footnotes .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/08-footnotes/slides.html"}
```markdown
## Per-slide footnotes

A claim that needs a citation.^[The footnote text.]

::: {.aside}
An aside and the footnotes share the bottom of the slide.
:::
```

Footnotes gather into a per-slide aside at the bottom of their own slide. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/08-footnotes)
::::

To keep footnotes at the end of the deck instead — as a final slide —
set `reference-location: document`:

```yaml
---
format:
  revealjs:
    reference-location: document
---
```

## Themes

Every deck starts from the `default` theme — a left-aligned, white theme tuned
to feel like Quarto. To restyle the whole deck, set `theme:` to one of the
built-in reveal.js themes (`dark`, `league`, `dracula`, `solarized`, and the
rest):

:::: {#demo-themes .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/09-themes/slides.html"}
```markdown
---
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: dark
---

## A dark slide

Content on a dark background.
```

The `theme:` option restyles the deck's background, text, and links at once;
this deck uses the built-in `dark` theme. `white` aliases to `default` and
`black` aliases to `dark`. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/09-themes)
::::

## Footer and logo

To repeat a line of text along the bottom of every slide, set `footer:`. To pin
an image to the corner of every slide, set `logo:`. Both live in the front
matter and apply to the whole deck.

:::: {#demo-footer-logo .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/10-footer-logo/slides.html"}
```markdown
---
format: revealjs
footer: "© 2026 Example Corp — [example.com](https://example.com)"
logo: logo.svg
---

## A slide

The footer and logo appear here, and on every other slide.
```

The footer sits centered and muted at the bottom of each slide and accepts
Markdown, so a link in it renders as a link; the logo sits in the corner. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/10-footer-logo)
::::

## Stretching images

When a slide's only image stands in a block of its own, Quarto sizes it to fill
the space the slide's other content leaves — reveal.js calls this `.r-stretch`,
and Quarto adds it automatically so a large image never overflows. A heading and
a line of explanation can sit alongside the image.

:::: {#demo-auto-stretch .embed-example-iframe file="/examples/presentations/11-auto-stretch/slides.html"}
```markdown
## A single image fills the slide

Here is our architecture:

![](diagram.svg)
```

A lone slide image stretches to fill the available space. To keep an image at
its natural size, set `auto-stretch: false`, give the image an explicit
`width`/`height`, or mark it `.nostretch`. [View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/11-auto-stretch)
::::
